texts.preamble: Mahesh S/O. Umashankar Gaud vs The State Of Maharashtra And Others on 19 June, 2019 Author: T.V. Nalawade Bench: T.V. Nalawade, K.K. Sonawane 1 Application 250 of 2019 In The High Court Of Judicature At Bombay Bench At Aurangabad Criminal Application No.250 of 2019 Mahesh S/o Umashankar Gaud. .. Applicant. Versus The State of Maharashtra And Others. .. Respondents.
texts.facts: In this State from 20-7-2018 in public interest the State Government has prevented manufacture, sale, storage, transportation etc. of Gutkha, panmasala, sainted betel-nuts, sainted tobacco and similar items. reason behind this prohibition is the expert opinion that these substances are causing cancer which is a killing disease. 3) The incident took place on 24-12-2018. On that day police of Markhel Police Station intercepted a truck container bearing No.UP-14-FT-7198 and found that in Tahsil Degloor, sainted tobacco was being carried under different names in this truck. The truck and the driver were brought to police station and information was given to the Food and Drugs Administration of the Government. Under a panchanama these articles were taken over and value of the articles was more than Rs.46 lakh. Samples were collected and after seizure of these articles report was given. It is contended that there is contravention of the provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and the rules made under the Act in the year 2011 for 3 Application 250 of 2019 which punishment is provided in the Act and also for commission of aforesaid offences under Indian Penal Code. 4) The learned counsel for the applicant, driver of the truck, submitted that tobacco was being transported from Uttar Pradesh to Bidar, Karnataka. He has produced tax invoices in respect of some of the materials which are shown to be seized. The said 4 Application 250 of 2019 notification is not challenged in the present proceeding and relief of only quashing of the F.I.R. is claimed. 6) Those proceedings were filed by the persons who were doing business of manufacture, supply and distribution of panmasala containing tobacco (popularly called as Gutkha) and panmasala containing other harmful substances like magnesium carbonate. This Court referred 5 Application 250 of 2019 to the decision of the Apex Court given in Criminal Appeal No.1195/2018 (State of Maharashtra & Others v. Sayyed Hassan) decided on 20-9-2018 and other decisions. In Writ Petition No.9865/2012 (cited supra) it was a case of a businessman that he was only transporting the material from Gujarat to Karnataka through Maharashtra and there was a challenge to the seizure of the goods and at that time there was notification dated 19-7-2012. No licence was obtained under the Act as such substance is treated as food article. Definition of "food business" contains transportation and so relief in respect of seized Gutkha was refused. In the subsequent decision viz. Writ Petition No.1631/2012 (cited supra) a Standing Order of 2012 was challenged.
texts.arguments: He submitted that under the notification in question of the Commissioner of Food and Drugs Administration, Maharashtra State, though there is ban on manufacture, storage, distribution, transportation or sale of tobacco which is either flavoured, sainted or mixed with any of the said adhesives under the provisions of section 30(2)(a) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act") there could not have been prohibition on transportation. He also submitted that in view of provisions of Articles 19, 301 and 304 of the Constitution of India, such prohibition order also could not have been issued. Admittedly, these articles are banned in Maharashtra under the aforesaid notification for the aforesaid purposes. The learned counsel for the applicant placed reliance on some observations made by the Apex Court in Civil Appeal Nos.10373-10374 of 2010 (State of Gujarat v. Jayeshbhai Kanjibhai Kalathiya) decided on 1-3-2019. This was in respect of transportation of sand from Gujarat when there was ban on taking the sand outside of the State due to scarcity of sand. It was legally excavated sand
